text:
Alex M: Hey all — quick onboarding qs. I started last Thursday as a remote hire. Two quick things: 1) when do my medical/dental benefits actually kick in? 2) We have a company holiday coming up next month — is that holiday pay prorated for new hires? Also my moving reimbursement receipts are ready — who should I send them to?

Jules HR: Welcome Alex 🎉. Quick answers: benefits eligibility is after 30 days and then the effective date is the first day of the following month. For example, if your 30th day lands in March, benefits start April 1. Holidays: we pro-rate holiday pay for folks who start after the cutoff in the company's holiday policy (it depends on payroll cutoff).

Sam R: Yep — for your specific start date I think you’ll be eligible but it might be pro-rated. I’ll check the cutoff doc and ping payroll. For moving reimbursement, upload receipts to the Relocation form in the People Ops portal and cc me so I can approve on my side.

People Ops: Hi Alex — welcome! A few helpful links and steps: 1) Benefits doc: <https://intranet.redwood.com/people-ops/benefits|Benefits & Eligibility> 2) Moving reimbursement: go to the People Ops portal -> Forms -> `Relocation Reimbursement`, attach receipts, submit. If your total reimbursement request is >$5,000 please include the relocation approval email in the notes and email people-ops@redwood.com. 3) Dependent verification: if you enroll dependents for medical/dental, please upload proof (marriage certificate, birth certificate, or insurance card) within 60 days of enrollment.

PayrollBot: Payroll summary: biweekly pay schedule. Next scheduled payday for new hires is the upcoming Friday (check Paystub in ADP). Holiday pay/pro-rate rules: payroll calculates prorated holiday pay for employees whose start date falls after the holiday eligibility cutoff for that pay period. See payroll FAQ: <https://intranet.redwood.com/payroll/faq|Payroll FAQ>.

Alex M: Thanks — super helpful. One more: my benefits debit card hasn’t arrived yet, should I expect a paper card or an e-card?

Jules HR: Cards typically ship within 7-10 business days after benefits become active. We also provide an e-card/ID that you can download earlier — check the carrier portal link in the Benefits doc. If it’s been longer after your effective date, ping us here and we’ll escalate.

People Ops: Also — for the holiday specifically, if payroll determines a pro-rate applies we’ll show it on your first paystub. If you want, @Sam R and I can run a quick estimate for you now if you DM your start date.

Alex M: Awesome — DMing you my start date now. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
